q1_issues.issue: The restrictive participial 'wrongly used' is placed in the rule premise as Skolem-function terms `(sk_use $x)`, but a premise must match existing atoms through a plain variable (as the donkey-anaphora relative clause does), so this restriction can never bind an ordinarily asserted use-event.

q2_gaps: 'as well as' as an NP coordinator (additive coordination of two objects) — the instruction set covers plain 'and' coordination and the additive focus particle 'as well', but never this coordinator, so its additive/scalar force has no assigned encoding

comma-offset adverbial participle ('Power, wrongly used, defeats ...') taken as a condition on the generic — participial modifiers are covered only as restrictive reduced relatives, with no guidance on whether a comma-set-off one restricts a rule or is asserted
notes: The rule form, the 0.9/0.9 TV with no QuantifierPhrase companion, Theme for 'use', the surface-form Manner filler 'wrongly' and the distributive split into two defeat events all follow the instruction set; only the premise's Skolem terms are off. Bare class fillers for the generic definites 'the oppressor' / 'the oppressed' are licensed by the non-specific-object clause of the existential section.
